reviews.review: if you like the movies  , gotta play the games.

Aliens: Fireteam Elite 
Play as a solider whos job is to hold fire until they die, there not really much fear or intense game play at all unless you play the game on an unforgiving difficulty which becomes unplayable due to the scaling system of points per arms. Its not really worth playing but who knows you might like it.

It is a fun Co-Op shooter game themed around the Aliens universe and you are one of 3 Marines that must complete missions in an Alien infested territory (+ others, but I will not give spoilers).

Pros:
- nice sound effects, recognisable for hardcore fans
- fairly decent customisation options, but will not compete with games like Tarkov or C.o.D.
- class-based characters that have various gameplay styles and strenghts (although some are more useful than others)
- a good choice for Aliens fans, where iconic elements are well-built in-game like acid blood, synthetics and the famous Pulse rifle with it's iconic sound
- did not encounter any visual or game breaking bugs on the current version of the game

Cons:
- a bit of a short campaign, with not many missions and an overpriced DLC for what it offers, but it is acceptable at 50% discount
- if your connection is a bit unstable, you get kicked out of the mission or you'll continue alone with 2 AI bots instead of your friends, if you quit to re-match with them, you also lose the challenge card if you activated one
- some pistol sounds may bug out and will fail to play (not game breaking, but it may be annoying to others)
- the sessions seems to be player-based and if the host is someone from far away or with bad connection, you will encounter issues like lag or rubber-banding

Fun TPS with multiple classes, gadgets and a lot of customizable weapons that feel good to use. 
The missions are fun but can feel repetitive after a few playthroughs since the enemy attacks happen always at the same places. The game remains challenging though at higher difficulties, becoming a bit technical to beat which is good if that is your thing.

The campaign's a bit short, like everyone says, but it's a surprisingly solid little shooter. Playing around with the different weapons, classes, and kits does change up the experience too, since at best you'll find a weapon that's "okay" for all situations. But the experimentation and the different combinations are fun to tinker with.

It's not going to be a groundbreaking experience or anything, but it's also not Aliens: Colonial Marines. The only actual complaint I have so far is that the characters are still just straight faced and dead-eyed while speaking and their mouths don't move. The decision's definitely a head scratcher, but it's been a long time since something like that is the biggest complaint I've had about a game in this franchise.
